root_cause: commands/_matchup_utils.py::_extract_full_name_comparison lets the second operand carry sample suffixes, but _resolve_comparison_player_phrase rejects any team alias anywhere inside it. AD forLakers therefore loses the second resolved player.
natural_query.py::_player_team_comparison protects oneplayer+team ambiguity only when no opponent exists. Adding opponentGSW bypasses that guard and silently falls back to one-playerfinder.

Question-form extraction resolves both names before compare, but _build_parse_state deliberately detects team only when no playerpair exists. Thus How did A and B compare forLakers... retains both players but silently drops the team restriction.

Existing player_compare.build_result(team,opponent,...) independently filters each player through canonical row team identity. Its existing structured route already computes the intended values; there is no missing calculation/data dependency.
source_checks: All3physical CSV SHA match verified inventory; player/game keys unique; selected5positive rows match exact canonical IDs/dates/actualteams, catalog home/away pair and reciprocal team-game identity. Totals and Decimal mean fractions were computed directly from CSV before checking engine results. No seasonwide participation or roster inference.
